basic_info: 14-year-old female with a two-year history of daily facial acne; mother is present.
present_illness: The patient is a 14-year-old female with a two-year history of daily facial acne. She reports having a lot of blackheads and whiteheads, especially on her forehead, and some small, erythematous papules on her cheeks and chin. The acne is not severe on her chest or back. The red bumps on her cheeks and chin are small, red, and raised, and have remained stable over time. She has not had any scarring or pain from it. She has been using Persa-Gel and washing her face regularly, and it’s helped a little, but not as much as she’d like. The worst flare was when she started playing sports in the fall because of the sweating. The patient uses a noncomedogenic moisturizer only when her skin feels dry, not every day.
past_history: No family history of acne or related skin conditions. Potential triggers include sweating from school sports in the fall. Uses SPF 30 sunscreen in the summer, a cleanser (sometimes Elf cleanser in the morning, Elf Super Clarity Cleanser at night), toner, Persa-Gel, and noncomedogenic moisturizer (only when her skin feels dry). No significant impact from diet or stress. The patient has not tried any other treatments besides Persa-Gel. No known history of antibiotic use or hormonal therapies. The patient does not believe her menstrual cycle or hormonal fluctuations are affecting her acne.
physical_exam: The patient has comedones (blackheads and whiteheads) predominantly on the forehead, cheeks, and chin. There are small, erythematous papules on the cheeks and chin. The red bumps are non-tender, non-itchy, and non-swollen. No signs of scarring, pain, itching, or swelling. No involvement of the chest or back.
aux_exam: No relevant laboratory or imaging studies have been performed.
